q: Is an electric bus lower carbon than a diesel bus on the Indian grid?
title: Electric vs diesel bus on the Indian grid
short: Compare per kilometre with your own figures: diesel litres per km times 2.68, against kWh at the depot meter per km times 0.710. On grid power the gap can be modest; renewable electricity bought with evidence widens it on the market-based method.
audience: Bus operators and electric bus depot managers in India comparing fleets

p: Diesel bus: litres per km from fuel records x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre.
Electric bus: kWh per km at the depot meter, including charger losses, x 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25.
Compare on the same routes and seasons.
If the depot buys renewable power through open access or certificates, report a market-based figure as well, with the evidence.

example.title: Worked example: per km (illustrative inputs)
lines: Diesel bus: 0.35 L per km x 2.68 = 0.938 kg CO2 per km
Electric bus: 1.2 kWh per km x 0.710 = 0.852 kg CO2 per km
Difference: 0.938 minus 0.852 = 0.086 kg CO2 per km on grid power
example.note: Consumption figures are illustrative; use your own fuel and meter records.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
